items.title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
items.excerpt: Helmholtz Institute (HIPS) researchers combined pretrained AI models with lab tests to design 76 new thiolation domains for nonribosomal peptide synthetase assembly lines; several worked in living cells and some tripled product yields.

items.title: AI reveals how a warming climate will intensify NZ's most extreme downpours
items.excerpt: A generative AI model trained on 140 years of regional climate simulations produced 15,000+ simulated years for New Zealand, showing 1-in-100-year daily rainfall intensifies about 9% per degree of warming.

items.title: Giving AI a 'crystal clear' view of the materials world by mapping geometry to text
items.excerpt: MIT researchers built a multimodal contrastive model that aligns 3D crystal structures with text descriptions, letting scientists retrieve materials by natural-language property queries; it surfaced promising solid-state lithium electrolyte candidates.

items.title: New materials library could help AI design better sodium-ion batteries
items.excerpt: University of Surrey researchers built a library of 28 sodium manganese oxide cathode compositions and trained a machine-learning model on the automated test data, as a seed dataset for AI-driven sodium-ion battery design.

items.title: Researchers develop conversational AI for self-driving labs
items.excerpt: KRICT researchers let scientists steer self-driving labs in plain language: an LLM turns expert guidance into structured priors for Bayesian optimization, and discards the guidance when data contradict it, cutting the experiments needed.

items.title: AI chatbots could help mental health but also reinforce harmful thinking
items.excerpt: Curtin University psychologist Warren Mansell proposes a framework in Digital Health linking a chatbot's effects to users' emotional state and goals, explaining how AI companions can both help and foster dependence or harmful thinking.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this AI-generated proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis has been unpacked by human experts; one mathematician called the implications 'staggering.'

items.title: Study: AI Could Speed Quantum Threats — And Help Build Defenses
items.excerpt: A new analysis argues AI could accelerate quantum threats to encryption, by speeding quantum algorithm and hardware progress, while also helping organizations prepare post-quantum defenses.

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A psychology study finds people draw a sharp line between human and AI consciousness even when both behave identically: participants rated the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human.

items.title: Physicists develop early warning system that predicts when an AI is about to go rogue
items.excerpt: Physicists derived a mathematical formula that tracks an AI model's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they happen, applying statistical-physics tools to language-model behavior.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research details Earth AI geospatial agents that combine Gemini reasoning with remote-sensing, population and environment foundation models to answer complex planetary-science and crisis-response questions.

items.title: Interspecies communication
items.excerpt: Part of MIT Technology Review's 'Impossible' issue: how machine learning is being used to decode animal communication, from whales to birds, and what it could reveal about the inner lives of other species.

items.title: Raman+NIR Spectra Improves Glucose Soft Sensing
items.excerpt: A multimodal soft-sensing framework fuses Raman and NIR spectra and benchmarks PLS, gradient-boosted trees, CNNs and temporal convolutional networks to monitor glucose in bioprocessing, easing a bottleneck for continuous manufacturing.

items.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
items.excerpt: Ai2's FairStress benchmark reveals demographic differences in how LLMs defend and explain their decisions, even when their final choices appear fair — a behavioral-science style probe of model reasoning.

items.title: Would You Read Your Partner's ChatGPT?
items.excerpt: A certified sex and relationship therapist describes a new kind of betrayal emerging in couples therapy: partners confiding in ChatGPT, and the psychology of reading a partner's AI chat history.
